title: ESE test corpus manifest
description: One entry per ESE database in the corpus. Paths are relative to the folder that holds manifest.json (the corpus root, e.g. the value of CRUSH_ESE_CORPUS).

id.description: Stable slug, unique in the manifest. Also the folder name under files/redist/ or files/local/.

artifact_detail.description: Free text when artifact_type is 'other' (e.g. 'UAL Current.mdb', 'CertLog.edb', 'Exchange priv1.edb', 'synthetic AllTypes').

redistributable.description: true only if the source terms allow redistribution. false => the file lives under files/local/ and is git-ignored; only this manifest entry is committed.

path.description: Relative to the corpus root, forward slashes.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the extracted database exactly as stored at 'path' (not of a .gz wrapper).

compressed_as.description: Set when the file at 'path' is stored compressed; sha256/size are then of the decompressed bytes.

sidecars.description: Transaction logs (.log/.jrs), checkpoint (.chk), flush map (.jfm) etc. extracted alongside the database.

licence.description: SPDX id where one exists (CC0-1.0, Apache-2.0, ...) or a short description of the terms.

image_name.description: File name of the source image/archive (e.g. 'cfreds_2015_data_leakage_pc.E01').

path_in_image.description: Path of the database inside the image, e.g. 'C:/Windows/System32/sru/SRUDB.dat'.

retrieved.description: ISO date the source was downloaded or the file was generated.

header.description: Fields read from the ESE file header (page 0) by tools/add_to_manifest.py.

signature_ok.description: bytes ef cd ab 89 at offset 4

file_type.description: uint32 at offset 12: 0 = database, 1 = streaming file

format_version.description: uint32 at offset 8, hex string, e.g. '0x620'

format_revision.description: uint32 at offset 232, hex string, e.g. '0x14'

page_size.description: uint32 at offset 236; 0 in very old files means 4096

reference.description: Expected results from an independent reference tool, run separately. Consumed by the opt-in Crush corpus test.
